exposure to emissions from burning of sugar cane induced acute inflammation of the tracheal mucosa and lung parenchyme in rats, and that these changes were more pronounced with longer periods of exposure to these emissions.
exposure to emissions from sugarcane burning induces acute focal and diffuse inflammatory reactions in the trachea lamina propria, with no loss in ciliated epithelial cells.
emissions from sugar cane fires induce acute inflammation and edema in the lung and tracheal tissues of Wistar rats, with no loss in ciliated epithelium in the trachea.

the effects of emissions from sugar-cane burning on inflammatory processes in the trachea, lung, and lung parenchyme.
the effects of exposure over time to emissions from sugar-cane burning on the tracts of the respiratory tract of rats.
the early effects of sugar cane burning on tissues of the traches and lungs of rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exposure to smoke from burning sugar cane for 21 days was the most intense, with the most severe effects on the tracheal and lung tissues.
the effects of sugar cane burning emissions are dependent upon the time of exposure.

exposure to sugar cane burning emissions for 21 days induced significant alterations in the tracheal and lung parenchyme, with a predominance of inflammatory processes in the trachea, while the lung parenchyme showed signs of acute and chronic inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the exposure to sugar cane burning emissions in the short term induces inflammatory changes in the trachea of Wistar rats, while exposure to emissions in the long term induces inflammatory changes and angiogenesis in the parenchyma.
the emissions from sugar cane burnings induce acute inflammation of the respiratory tract and lungs, which may be related to the presence of toxic compounds in the smoke.

the exposure to sugar cane burning emissions in rats for a short period of time (7 days) induced a greater inflammatory process, whereas exposure for 21 days resulted in more intense collagen deposition in the tracheal tissue and angiogenesis in the pulmonary parenchyma.

the effects of sugar cane burning on respiratory tissues of Wistar rats are dependent on the period of exposure.
exposure to emissions from burning of sugar cane for 21 days caused more severe histopathological changes in the trachea than in the lung paren-chyma.

exposure to emissions from burning sugar cane for 21 days induced more intense inflammation and collagen deposition in the tracheal tissues and increased angiogenesis in the parenchyma, which may be related to the duration of exposure to these pollutants.
